subject: Mediform integration fit — SDK impact, streaming & funcall checklist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Leah Brooks <leah.brooks@mediform.com>, Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@mediform.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Mediform integration fit — SDK impact, streaming & funcall checklist

Hi Leah / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap while it’s fresh and a proposed list of engineering asks so we can scope a tight POC:

Key pain points you stated
- Current assistant returns are too slow for triage workflows (p95 latency spikes during batch ingestion).
- Relevance drop for long patient histories — ranking/order matters for clinician UX.
- Need strongly structured, validated outputs (EHR fields) for downstream ingestion (no manual parsing).
- Security/compliance and auditability: evidence of data access controls and vault/KMS integration required.

Goals for the POC
1) 1-week functional POC demonstrating: streaming responses for progressive UI, structured JSON outputs matching Mediform schema (see attached MVP scope), and an embeddings-based rerank for encounter-history retrieval.
2) p95 generation latency <= 450ms on typical 512-token prompt mix; cost estimate for 10k monthly active clinicians.
3) Integration pattern for function_call hooks that create discrete EHR write intents (we don’t want to rely on fuzzy text parsing).

SDK / product implications we recommend for the POC
- Streaming: enable chunked partial responses plus a final structured payload. SDK should provide onChunk/onComplete hooks and an optional token-level latency metric.
- Function calling: a strongly typed function_call API that returns both the call payload and a ConfidenceScore. Mediform will reject low-confidence function outputs.
- Structured outputs: support for JSON Schema validation server-side (or a schema param in the generation call) so outputs are validated before returning to UI.
- Embeddings + rerank: pipeline to index encounter vectors (embedding dimension & model specified) and an example reranker that merges semantic score + recency weight.
- KV / prefix caching: for repeated clinician prompts, KV cache to avoid re-computation for stable context windows.

Operational asks
- We’ll need an isolated tenant for the POC (dedicated instance or VPC-private deployment) and SOC2 artifacts — attached our SLA + privacy doc for reference.
- Rate limits and throttles: ability to set per-project concurrency and a per-user token cap for safety.

Proposed next steps
1) We (Redwood) deliver a short tech brief + POC plan (Fri, Jun 11).
2) Mediform to confirm security contact and procurement timeline (are you able to share who will handle the SOW/PO?).
3) Kickoff meeting for engineering alignment next Tue/Wed (Jun 15/16).

Attachments: Mediform-MVP-scope.xlsx (scope + JSON schema), redwood-inference-privacy-sla.pdf

Thanks — I’ll draft the POC plan and put proposed milestone dates into the drive link I shared.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Leah Brooks <leah.brooks@mediform.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Nguyen <t.nguyen@mediform.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mediform integration fit — SDK impact, streaming & funcall checklist

Jonas —

This is great, thanks for the clear checklist. A few clarifications from our side:

- Timeline: we like the compact approach. Procurement expects to review a short SOW and an indicative budget by next week; can you include a ballpark monthly run-rate for the POC (0.5–1.0M tokens/month)?
- Function calling: we need deterministic outputs for WriteIntent functions. If ConfidenceScore < 0.8, outputs must be marked for human review. Is that something the SDK can surface?
- Structured outputs: our schema has nested arrays for medications and allergies; please confirm the SDK/server will validate arrays and return a clear validation error taxonomy so UI can highlight which fields failed.
- Security: attached is a short SOC2 excerpt and our security lead (Tom) will run through a quick set of infra questions — expect a short questionnaire this week.

Tom and I also flagged a procurement constraint: Mediform requires a named SOW with acceptance criteria before procurement signs the PO.

We’re happy to do the kickoff Tue Jun 15 at 10am PT; does that work for your team?

Attaching: Mediform-SOC2-excerpt.pdf

Thanks — Leah
Leah Brooks
Director of Product | Mediform
leah.brooks@mediform.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Mediform integration fit — SDK impact, streaming & funcall checklist

Marissa — quick internal note (forwarding Leah’s reply):

Summary for pricing & engineering:
- Leah asked for ballpark monthly run-rate for 0.5–1.0M tokens; we should present two options: hosted (variable token pricing) and a dedicated POC pool estimate.
- Function_call deterministic gating: they need ConfidenceScore threshold behavior and error taxonomy surfaced by SDK — this will likely require a tiny server-side wrapper that annotates outputs and returns validationFailure reasons.
- Validation taxonomy: Engineering should return error codes (e.g., schema.array_missing, schema.enum_mismatch) that UI can map.
- Security: Tom will send questionnaire; field team needs SOC2 evidence and confirmation we can spin up an isolated tenant for the POC.

Proposed internal asks:
1) Can we commit to a POC SOW template with acceptance criteria (I’ll draft) and two pricing options?
2) E2E demo candidate: we should prepare a small node/python sample that shows streaming + function_call + JSON schema validation in <30 lines.

If you’re good, I’ll draft the SOW & two-tier pricing and share for review this afternoon.

— Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Hi Leah / Tom — looping back with agreed next steps and commitments from Redwood: 

Committed deliverables this week
- POC SOW (Jonas to draft) — will include explicit acceptance criteria and example test prompts that must pass schema validation.
- Indicative pricing: two options (hosted POC rates; dedicated POC reserved pool) with redacted T&Cs for procurement to review.
- Tech sample: minimal Python + Node examples that show streaming onChunk/onComplete, a function_call with ConfidenceScore, and server-side JSONSchema validation.
- Isolated tenant confirmation: we can provide a VPC-private sandbox for the POC and will include SOC2 excerpt and audit logs guidance.

Requested from Mediform
- Procurement contact and preferred PO timing (we’ll attach a template SOW to speed review).
- Any additional fields in the JSON schema that are mandatory for acceptance (please mark in the spreadsheet).
- Tom: if you can send the security questionnaire link, we’ll route to security for a rapid turnaround.

Suggested kickoff: Tue Jun 15 — 10:00am PT. I’ll send calendar invites and include engineering (runtime lead) + solutions.
